messages:
maria: Hey team — running into a weird `poetry add`/`poetry lock` hang when adding the python SDK (redwood). It sits on "Resolving dependencies (this can take a while)" for 10+ minutes and CI times out. Anyone seen this?
kevin: Yeah saw something like that earlier. Which SDK package name/version are you trying to add? poetry version?
maria: Using poetry 1.4.2 locally, CI uses 1.5.1. Trying: `poetry add redwood-sdk==0.11.0` (we pinned for reproducible builds).
alex: Can you paste your pyproject deps? sometimes typing-extensions / python constraint causes solver explosion.
maria: Here's the minimal pyproject snippet:```[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.9"
fastapi = "^0.95"
redwood-sdk = "0.11.0"
typing-extensions = "^4.5"
```
It starts resolving and then CPU spikes and nothing helpful in logs.
sasha: Interesting — our monorepo saw poetry spend ages when a new package had broad optional extras that pulled in conflicting constraints. Does redwood-sdk declare extras like `[http2]` or platform markers?
maria: I inspected the wheel metadata (downloaded sdist from PyPI). It declares optional extras: `http2`, `torch`, `dev`. No platform markers.
kevin: Could be the combination of `typing-extensions` and `python = ^3.9` with a wheel built for py3.11 only — solver tries many back-and-forth combos. Two quick repros: 1) poetry 1.4.2 local -> hangs; 2) pip install works fine (installs wheel).
alex: Can you try `poetry add --no-root --lock` or `poetry lock --no-update` to see if lockfile generation is the bottleneck?
maria: Tried `poetry lock --no-update` — it still spins. `poetry add redwood-sdk --no-dev` same. `pip install redwood-sdk==0.11.0` works locally (installs prebuilt wheel).
sasha: Does your CI use constrained-platform wheel building? sometimes pip will pick a manylinux wheel which is fine; poetry's resolver tries to pick compatible ranges and stalls.
kevin: Two workarounds we've used: 1) pin direct transitive deps that are common conflict sources (e.g., typing-extensions) in pyproject to reduce search space; 2) add `[[package]]` entries manually to the lockfile as a stopgap (ugly).
maria: Pinned `typing-extensions = "^4.5.0"` and finally `poetry lock` completed in ~30s. So that confirms solver blowup. But we shouldn't have to pin often.
alex: Could be a packaging-side issue — if redwood-sdk declares very loose ranges for some dependencies, resolving in presence of other packages explodes. Can you open a minimal repro repo and share?
maria: I made a tiny repro: https://github.com/redwood-internal/poetry-repro (private link). Steps: `git clone ... && poetry install`. Repros on both mac and ubuntu.
sasha: I'll triage: quick checklist — (a) verify redwood-sdk's metadata (`pip index versions`, `packaging`), (b) check extras which pull in `httpx[http2]` -> h2 and dependencies, (c) attempt with poetry 1.5.x because resolver improvements landed.
kevin: FYI: upstream poetry 1.5 changed resolver heuristics; we saw fewer hangs. Try CI with 1.5.2.
maria: Switched CI to poetry 1.5.2 — lock completes faster but still sometimes spikes. The repro shows non-deterministic behavior.
alex: I'll download the published wheel and show the dependency metadata:```Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 0.11.0
Requires-Dist: httpx; extra == 'http'
Requires-Dist: httpx[http2]; extra == 'http2'
Requires-Dist: typing-extensions (>=4.1)
```
That `typing-extensions (>=4.1)` plus our `typing-extensions ^4.5` shouldn't be bad, but if other deps allow older versions the solver tests many combos.
sasha: Could you try `poetry add redwood-sdk --extras ""` (no extras) to avoid optional deps?
maria: `poetry add redwood-sdk --extras ""` still triggers long resolve. But `pip install redwood-sdk==0.11.0` remains quick.
kevin: This suggests poetry resolver is the bottleneck, not wheel packaging. Two action items: (1) DevEx creates a short guide/workaround for customers hitting slow poetry resolves (pin common transitive deps, use pip fallback, upgrade poetry), (2) engineering (SDK) audits our setup for overly-loose ranges or unnecessary extras causing combinatorial explosion.
alex: I'll open an internal issue: INFRA-8463. Include repro, profiler output, and suggestion to tighten some ranges.
maria: Filed INFRA-8463, assigned to eng-runtime. Also added a short note to README: "If `poetry lock` hangs, try upgrading poetry to 1.5.x or pip installing the wheel as a temporary workaround."
sasha: For SDK side — can we modestly pin typing-extensions to `>=4.5,<5` in metadata or in the sdist metadata? That may help consumers.
alex: We should avoid forcing consumers, but a more narrow lower bound in setup.cfg/pyproject may reduce solver work. I'll propose `typing-extensions>=4.5` (which we already have) and ensure we don't rely on unstable open ranges elsewhere. Also add CI test that does a fresh `poetry lock` in a minimal env to catch regressions.
kevin: One more DX note: docs should include "If you're on Poetry and see long resolves: try pip install wheel first, or pin `typing-extensions` in your pyproject." I'll draft.
maria: Thanks all. Workarounds in place for our app CI. Leaving thread open for SDK packaging follow-ups. dev-bot: Incident INFRA-8463 created by alex, severity: low, assignee: eng-runtime.
